parts.text:
5
What is the definition of acceleration?
A
the rate of change of displacement
B
the rate of change of kinetic energy
C
the rate of change of momentum
D
the rate of change of velocity

hints: Notice each option says rate of change of a different quantity: displacement, kinetic energy, momentum and velocity.
Recall the chain displacement to velocity to acceleration, where each is the time-rate of change of the previous one.
Check which rate gives units of $\text{m s}^{-2}$ and which rate is linked to force in $F = ma$ to separate velocity change from momentum change.
walkthrough: List the four quantities offered: displacement $s$, kinetic energy $E_k$, momentum $p = mv$, and velocity $v$.
Recall that velocity is defined as rate of change of displacement, $v = \Delta s / \Delta t$.
Recall that acceleration describes how quickly velocity itself changes with time, $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$ with unit $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
Distinguish the close distractor: rate of change of momentum $\Delta p / \Delta t$ equals resultant force, not acceleration.
Therefore the definition matching acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. This is option D.

A.explanation: The rate of change of displacement is velocity, $v = \Delta s / \Delta t$, not acceleration.

B.explanation: Kinetic energy changes when work is done, but its rate of change is related to power, not the definition of acceleration.

C.explanation: The rate of change of momentum equals resultant force from Newton's second law, not acceleration.

D.explanation: Acceleration is defined as $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$, the rate of change of velocity in $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
